subject: Mutual Action Plan: evaluation -> acceptance -> billing start / PO & payment terms

Subject: Mutual Action Plan: evaluation -> acceptance -> billing start / PO & payment terms

Hi Elaine / Patrick —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation gates, acceptance criteria, and the commercial milestones that trigger invoicing. High level:

- 4‑week evaluation (pilot) with technical acceptance tests (see section 2)
- Staged ramp: pilot -> limited production -> GA (full production) with monthly commit tiers
- Pricing: list price + volume-based ramp discounts tied to committed monthly throughput
- Billing start: preferred by Redwood is billing-on-acceptance (production go‑live); open to aligning to PO effective date if required

Two questions for you to confirm so we can finalize the MAP and SOW:
1) Do you require the vendor invoice to be tied to a submitted PO? If yes, will you provide a PO number before the evaluation or only upon contract signature?
2) Payment terms: our standard is Net30; we can accommodate Net60 with a modest pricing adjustment (we propose 5% off list for Net60 coupled with the 6‑month committed ramp).

I attached: MAP-FTL-2027-04.pdf (draft MAP) and Redwood-SOW-draft.docx (SOW skeleton). I copied Ben (sales ops) and Marissa (account lead) to confirm billing cadence and discount mechanics.

Next steps: Elaine, if you can confirm PO timing and preferred payment terms by end of week, Ben and I will finalize the pricing table and send an updated MAP for signature.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, West Coast
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the MAP and the clear breakdown. Quick answers from our side:

1) PO: Our procurement requires a PO for any vendor spend. We can issue a provisional PO to cover the evaluation if needed, but the standard is to issue a PO at contract signature. We will confirm whether a provisional PO is feasible — I have flagged this with procurement.
2) Payment terms: our accounts-payable team defaults to Net60. We understand commercial trade-offs; please send any details on discount vs term and any minimum commitment requirements.

Two small asks: can the MAP include a clause that billing will not start until the acceptance checklist is met (not just after a date)? And can you add an attachment that lists the acceptance tests we ran during the demo?

Cheers,
Elaine

Kim / Marissa —

Thanks Elaine for the quick reply (cc’d). A few notes from Sales Ops / Finance:

- Net30 is our standard. We can accept Net60 but will require a commercial offset (we typically take 3–6% depending on volume). For this deal size band I recommend 5% discount for Net60 if FTL signs a 6‑month minimum with the staged monthly commit (see pricing table in the attached SOW).
- Billing start: we are comfortable making billing contingent on the acceptance checklist. Operationally we request a signed acceptance form (one‑page) at the end of the test window or a confirmed production go‑live note from your platform lead. That acceptance form will be the invoice trigger.
- PO handling: if procurement can provide a provisional PO for the pilot we will be able to invoice the evaluation period; otherwise we can invoice retroactively once a PO is issued, but payable under the agreed terms. Note: retro invoicing can complicate cloud credits and trial allowances.

I attached an example PO template (FTL-PO-template.pdf) and a short acceptance form we use internally. Kimberly / Marissa — if we agree to Net60 + 5% discount, update the MAP pricing line and I’ll prepare the final commercial redline.

Ben

All —

Thanks for the clarity, Patrick. Proposed compromise from commercial:

- We will accept Net60 and monthly invoicing for FinTech Labs.
- In exchange, Redwood will extend a 5% billing credit (applied as a recurring discount) provided FTL commits to the 6‑month ramp schedule in the MAP with minimum monthly commit tiers outlined in Section 4.
- Billing start = invoice trigger is the signed acceptance form (production go‑live or signed checklist at the end of the pilot). For the evaluation pilot we will accept the provisional PO number on the first invoice; once the final PO is issued we will reference it on subsequent invoices.
- If the ramp commits are not met in month 3, the discount will be pro‑rated and revert to list pricing going forward.

Kimberly: I updated the MAP pricing table and the small acceptance form. Attaching the updated MAP (MAP-FTL-2027-04.pdf v2). Elaine / Patrick — please review the acceptance wording in section 2 and the ramp tiers in section 4. If that looks good, we can convert to final SOW and send for signature via DocuSign.

Cheers,

Subject: Final MAP & next steps for PO / invoicing cadence

Hi Elaine / Patrick —

Thanks for the quick review and for agreeing to the provisional PO path. Per the agreed commercial summary below (and attached MAP v2 / SOW):

- Payment terms: Net60 accepted. Redwood will apply a 5% recurring discount contingent on the 6‑month ramp commitment (monthly minimums in Section 4).
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices referencing the provisional PO for the pilot; subsequent invoices will include the final PO number once procurement provides it.
- Invoice trigger: signed acceptance form (production go‑live or pilot acceptance checklist). Redwood will not bill before acceptance unless a provisional PO is used for pilot invoicing.
- PO template: attached FTL-PO-template.pdf — please confirm the provisional PO number and we will attach it to the first pilot invoice.

Next actions:
1) Patrick / Elaine: confirm provisional PO number and copy accounts-payable on that PO so we can send the first invoice when the pilot begins.
2) FinTech Labs: confirm the platform lead (for acceptance sign-off) so we have a contact for the acceptance form.
3) Marissa / Ben: I’ll route the final SOW to DocuSign after we get confirmation on the provisional PO.

Appreciate the collaboration — aiming to start the pilot week of May 10.

Best,
